newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr as RBI stays away.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr as RBI stays away.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady at 35.76/77 against the dollar on Tuesday in the absence of any market-moving factors, dealers said.

The rupee moved in a tight range of 35.76/77 throughout the day as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the State Bank of India (SBI), whose dollar purchases usually move the market, were not active on Tuesday, they said.
The rupee saw a high of 35.7600 and a low 35.7725 with most deals struck at 35.765 and 770 levels, dealers said.
"When the market is dominated by the absence or presence of the central bank, the outcome is nightmarish for traders," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
During April/May 1997, the RBI capped the rupee's rise at 35.75 by buying $2.0 billion at rates between 35.75 and 35.88.
But in June, RBI was buying dollars at rates of 35.77-35.80. "RBI seems to be fighting a losing battle," a dealer said.
Dealers said forecasts of falling export growth and widening trade deficit in the second half of 1997/98 (April-March) had no impact on the market.

The forward dollar market was steady and dull for most of Tuesday. "There was some paying (of premiums to buy forward dollars) after an auction of seven-year securities to raise 20 billion rupees on June 17 was announced," a dealer said.
The six-month annualised forward dollar premium closed steady at 4.42 percent.
